claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The Artemis II crew is returning from a 10-day lunar flyby.
The Artemis II crew will be recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
Splashdown coverage is live on NASA's YouTube channel, Netflix, and NASA+ beginning around 6:30 p.m. EDT.
Artemis II return sequence includes service module separation at 4:33 p.m. PDT (7:33 p.m. EDT) on April 10.
Artemis II return sequence includes entry interface (beginning of re-entry) at 4:53 p.m. PDT (7:53 p.m. EDT) on April 10.
Artemis II return sequence includes parachute deployment and splashdown at ~5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT) on April 10.
